properties.name: Lake Chad
properties.summary: Shallow endorheic lake shared with Chad, Niger, and Cameroon; size varies seasonally and has shrunk dramatically since the 1960s.
properties.description: Lake Chad once covered more than 25,000 km²; open water is now a fraction of that, replaced by marshes and receding shorelines. Nigerian shoreline is mainly in Borno (and historically Yobe). The lake still supports fishing, recession agriculture, and transhumant pastoralism, and is a focus of the Lake Chad Basin Commission.
properties.areaNote: ~1,350 km² open water (highly variable; far below 1960s extent)
properties.usage: Fishing, pastoralism, flood-recession farming, cross-border trade.
properties.ecology: Wetland birds, seasonal inundation, desertification pressure, invasive typha in some channels.
properties.climate: Sahel; rainfall decline and irrigation upstream affect inflows (Chari–Logone dominate).
properties.significance: UNESCO concern over shrinkage; security and livelihood hotspot of the basin.
properties.highlights: ["Shared by four countries","Severe 20th-century shrinkage","Livelihoods for millions in the basin"]

properties.name: Kainji Lake
properties.summary: Reservoir on the Niger created by Kainji Dam (1968); Nigeria's largest man-made lake.
properties.description: Kainji Dam was a flagship independent-era hydropower project. The lake drowned settlements and created a fishery and a national park (Kainji Lake National Park) on adjoining shores. Generation has varied with river flow and plant maintenance.
properties.usage: Hydroelectric power, fishing, limited navigation, tourism (park).
properties.ecology: Reservoir fishery; drawdown agriculture; wildlife in the national park.
properties.significance: First large Nigerian hydro dam; Power State identity of Niger.
properties.highlights: ["1968 Kainji Dam","Largest reservoir in Nigeria","National park shoreline"]

properties.name: Lagos Lagoon
properties.summary: Barrier-island lagoon behind Lagos; linked to the Atlantic through creeks and the harbour.
properties.description: The lagoon is the water body that made Lagos a port city. It receives Ogun/Osun drainage, urban wastewater, and sand-mining pressure. Water transport (Lagos Waterways) and fishing remain active despite pollution and siltation.
properties.usage: Fishing, sand mining, urban drainage, ferry transport, port access.
properties.ecology: Brackish water, mangroves (degraded), urban pollution hotspots.
properties.significance: Historic harbour of Eko; Lekki–Lagos urban waterfront.
properties.highlights: ["Made Lagos a port","Ferry network","Urban environmental pressure"]
